title: A clockwise rectangle on a p–V diagram
caption: The gas expands at 300 kPa (area under the top edge 300 J) and is compressed at 100 kPa (100 J given back), so the net work done by the gas is the enclosed area: 300 − 100 = 200 J. A clockwise cycle on p–V gives positive net work. This is the lesson's 1–3 × 10⁵ Pa, 1–2 L example.
alt: p–V rectangle with corners at (1 L, 100 kPa), (1 L, 300 kPa), (2 L, 300 kPa) and (2 L, 100 kPa) traversed clockwise; enclosed area 200 J.
description: The horizontal axis is volume in litres, the vertical axis pressure in kPa.
Clockwise from the bottom left: heated at constant volume from 100 to 300 kPa, expands at 300 kPa from 1 to 2 L, cooled at constant volume, compressed at 100 kPa.
Work done by the gas on the way across the top: 300 × (2 − 1) = 300 J; work done on it on the way back: 100 J.
Net work done per cycle = enclosed area = 200 J.
